ποιέω.long: (a) I make, manufacture, construct, (b) I do, act, cause.
ποιέω.sd: to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct)
ποιέω.kj: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield
ποιέω.der: apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary;
ποιέω.as:
ποιέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for a great variety of words, but chiefly for עשׂה;]
1.to make, produce, create, cause: c. acc. rei, Mt 17:4, Mk 9:5, Jo 9:11, Ac 9:39, Ro 9:20, al.; of God as Creator (c. acc. pers. also), Mt 19:4, Mk 10:6, Lk 11:40, Ac 4:24, He 1:2, al.; like Heb. עשׂה, absol. = ἐργάζομαι, to work, Mt 20:12 (cf. Ru 2:19; so AV, but v. infr.), Re 13:5, R, mg. (but v. infr.); σκάνδαλα, Ro 16:17; εἰρήνην, Eph 2:15, Ja 3:18; ἐπίστασιν, Ac 24:12; συστροφήν, Ac 23:12; c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Lk 1:68, Ac 15:3; with nouns expressing action or its accomplishment, forming a periphr. for the cogn. verb: ὁδόν π. (cl. ὁ ποιεῖσθαι), to go on, advance, Mk 2:23; πόλεμον, Re 11:7, al.; ἐκδίκησιν, Lk 18:7, 8; ἐνέδραν, Ac 25:3; κρίσιν, Jo 5:27, Ju 15; ἔργα, Jo 5:36, al.; σημεῖα (τέρατα καὶ σ.), Jo 2:23 and freq., Ac 2:22, al.; so also mid. ποιεῖσθαι: μονήν, Jo 14:23; πορείαν, Lk 13:22; κοινωνίαν, Ro 15:26; of food, to make ready, prepare: δεῖπνον, Mk 6:21, al.; δοχήν, Lk 5:2914:13; γάμους, Mt 22:2; of time, to spend (cl.): ὥραν, Mt 20:12, RV (but v. supr. and cf. McN, in l.); μῆνας, Re 13:5, R, txt. (cf. Swete, in l.; but v. supr.); ἐνιαυτόν, Ja 4:13; c. acc. seq. ἐκ, Jo 2:15, al.; c. acc. et acc. pred., Mt 3:312:16, Mk 1:33:12, Jo 5:11, al.; c. adv., καλῶς, Mk 7:37; ἑορτὴν π. (Dem., Ex 23:16, al.), Ac 18:21, Rec.; πάσχα, Mt 26:18; to make or offer a sacrifice (Plat., Xen., al.; Jb 42:8, III Ki 11:33; so some understand τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, Lk 22:19, but v. Abbott, Essays, 110 ff.); seq. ἵνα (WM, 422 f.; M, Pr., 228), Jo 11:37, Col 4:16, Re 3:9.
2.to do, perform, carry out, execute: absol., c. adv., καλῶς π., Mt 12:12, I Co 7:37, 38, Ja 2:19; id. seq. ptcp. (cl.; v. M, Pr., 228), Ac 10:33, Phl 4:14, II Pe 1:19, III Jo 6; οὕτως, Mt 24:46, Lk 9:15, al.; ὡς (καθώς), Mt 1:2421:6, al.; ὁμοίως, Lk 3:11; ὡσαύτως, Mt 20:5; c. ptcp., ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα, I Ti 1:13; c. acc. rei: τί interrog., Mt 12:3, Mk 2:25, Lk 6:2, al.; τοῦτο, Mt 13:28, Mk 5:32, Lk 22:19 (WH om.; v. supr., ref. to Abbott, Essays), Ro 7:20, al.; with nouns expressing command or regulation: τ. νόμον (not as in cl., to make a law), Jo 7:19, Ga 5:3 (cf. in LXX, Jos 22:5, I Ch 22:12, al.); τ. ἐντολάς, Mt 5:19; similarly with other nouns expressing conduct: τ. δικαιοσύνην, Mt 6:1, al.; τ. ἀλήθειαν, Jo 3:21, al., etc.; c. dupl. acc., Mt 27:22, Mk 15:12; c. acc. rei et dat. pers. (commod., incomm.; rare in cl.), Mt 7:12, Mk 5:19, 20, Lk 1:49, Jo 9:26, al.
SYN.: πράσσω, q.v. The general distinction between the two words is that between particular action and its habitual performance (cf. Tr., Syn., § xcvi; Westc. on Jo 3:21; ICC on Ro 1:32).

ποῦ.sd: as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality
ποῦ.der: genitive case of an interrogative pronoun (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as G4225 (πού) used with the rising slide of inquiry);
ποῦ.as:
ποῦ,
interrog. adv.,
[in LXX for אַי, אַיֵּה, אָנָה;]
1. prop., where?: Mt 2:226:17, Mk 14:12, 14, Lk 17:17, 3722:9, 11, Jo 1:397:118:[10], 199:1211:34; ποῦ (ἐστιν), indicating that the subject in question is not to be found, Lk 8:25, Ro 3:27, I Co 1:2012:17, 1915:55, Ga 4:15, II Pe 3:4; ποῦ φανεῖται, I Pe 4:18.
2. = ὅπου (WM, 640; Bl., § 50, 5): c. indic., Mt 2:4, Mk 15:47, Jo 1:4011:5720:2, 13, 15, Re 2:13; c. subjc., Mt 8:20, Lk 9:5812:17.
3. In colloq. (as in Eng.) = ποῖ, whither: in direct questions, Jo 7:359:1213:3616:5; in indir. quest., Jo 3:88:1412:3514:5, He 11:8, I Jo 2:11.†

ποιμαίνω.long: I shepherd, tend, herd; hence: I rule, govern.
ποιμαίνω.sd: to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser)
ποιμαίνω.as:
ποιμαίνω
(< ποιμήν), [in LXX chiefly for רעה;]
to act as shepherd, tend flocks: Lk 17:7; c. acc., ποίμνην, I Co 9:7. Metaph., to tend, shepherd, govern: c. acc., Mt 2:6(LXX), Jo 21:16, Ac 20:28, I Pe 5:2, Ju 12, Re 2:277:1712:519:15.†
SYN.: βόσκω, q.v.

πορεύομαι.sd: to traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.);
πορεύομαι.kj: --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk
πορεύομαι.der: middle voice from a derivative of the same as G3984 (πεῖρα);
πορεύομαι.as:
πορεύω,
(< πόρος, a ford, a passage), [in LXX chiefly for הלךְ;]
in cl. (the act. becomes obsolete in late Gk.; v. M, Pr., 162), to cause to go over, carry, convey. Mid. (always in LXX and NT), -ομαι, to go, proceed, go on one's way: c. acc., ὁδόν, Ac 8:39; seq. ἐκεῖθεν, Mt 19:15; ἐντεῦθεν, Lk 13:31; ἀπό, Mt 25:41, Lk 4:42; εἰς, Mt 2:20, Mk 16:12, Lk 1:39, Jo 7:35, al; εἰς εἰρήνην (cf. I Ki 1:17). Lk 7:50; ἐν εἰρήνῃ, Ac 16:36; ἐπί, c. acc., Mt 22:9, Ac 25:12, al; ἕως, Ac 23:23; οὗ, Lk 24:28, I Co 16:6; πρός, c. acc. pers., Mt 25:9, Lk 11:5, al.; κατὰ τ. ὁδόν, Ac 8:36; διά, c. gen., Mt 12:1, Mk 9:30; c. inf., Lk 2:3, Jo 14:2; σύν, Lk 7:6, al.; ἵνα, Jo 11:11; absol., Mt 2:9, Lk 7:8, Jo 4:50, Ac 5:20, al.; ptcp., πορευθείς (on the pass. form of the aor., v. M, Pr., 161 f.), redundant (as in Heb. and Aram.; V. M, Pr., 231; Dalman, Words, 21), Mt 2:8, Lk 7:22, al. Metaph. (cf. Soph., O.T., 884; Xen., Cyr., 2, 2, 24, al),
(a) like οἴχομαι in cl., as euphemism for θνήσκω (so הלךְ in Ge 15:2); Lk 22:22 and perh. also 13:33 (v. Field, Notes, 66);
(b) in ethical sense (De 19:9, Ps 14:2, al; cf. M, Pr., 112; Kennedy, Sources, 107): seq. ἐν, Lk 1:6, I Pe 4:3, II Pe 2:19; κατά, c. acc., II Pe 3:3, Ju 16, 18; c. dat. (Bl., § 38, 3), Ac 9:3114:16, Ju 11;
(c) of disciples or partisans (Jg 2:12, III Ki 11:10, Si 46:10): seq. ὀπίσω, c. gen. pers., Lk 21:8 (cf. δια-, εἰς-, (-μαι), ἐκ- (-μαι), ἐν- (-μαι), ἐπι- (-μαι), παρα- (-μαι), προ-, προσ- (-μαι), συν- (-μαι)).

πολύς.sd: (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely
πολύς.kj: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous, sore, straitly
πολύς.der: including the forms from the alternate ;
πολύς.as:
πολύς, πολλή, πολύ,
[in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms;]
1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Ac 11:21; ὄχλος, Mk 5:24; θερισμός, Mt 9:37; χόρτος, Jo 6:10; χρόνος, Mt 25:19; γογγυσμός, Jo 7:12; πόνος, Col 4:13; δόξα, Mt 24:30; σιγή, Ac 21:40; pl., προφῆται, Mt 13:17; ὄχλοι, Mt 4:25; δαιμόνια, Mk 1:34; δυνάμεις, Mt 7:22,
2. As subst., pl. masc., πολλοί, many (persons): Mt 7:22, Mk 2:2, al.; c. gen. partit., Mt 3:7, Lk 1:16, al.; seq. ἐκ, Jo 7:31, Ac 17:12; c. art., οἱ π., the many, Mt 24:12, Ro 12:5, I Co 10:17, 33, II Co 2:17; opp. to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Ro 5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Mt 13:3, Mk 5:26, al.; acc. with adverbial force, Mk 1:45, Ro 16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), I Co 16:12, Ja 3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Lk 12:48; adverbially, Mk 12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (gen. pret.), Mt 26:9; c. compar. (Bl., § 44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, II Co 8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, Jo 4:41.
Compar.,
πλείων,
neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (v. WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater;
1. as adj.: Jo 15:2, Ac 18:20, He 3:3; seq. παρά, He 11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ?); pi., Ac 13:31, al.; c. gen. compar., Mt 21:36; c. num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Ac 4:2224:11, al.
2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Ac 19:3227:12, I Co 10:515:6; also (Bl., § 44, 3) others, more, the more: II Co 2:64:15, Phl 1:14; πλείονα, Lk 11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Mt 20:10, II Ti 3:9; c. gen. comp., Mk12:43, Lk 21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Mt 12:41; adverbially, Ac 4:1720:924:4.
3. As adv.,πλεῖον: seq. ἤ, Lk 9:13; c. gen. comp., Mt 5:20; πλείω: c. num., Mt 26:53.
Superl.,
πλεῖστος, -η, -ον,
(a) prop., most: Mt 11:2021:8; adverbially, τὸ π., I Co 14:27;
(b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mk 4:1.

πόλις.long: a city, the inhabitants of a city.
πόλις.sd: a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size)
πόλις.der: probably from the same as G4171 (πόλεμος), or perhaps from G4183 (πολύς);
πόλις.as:
πόλις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for עִיר;]
a city: Mt 2:23, Mk 1:45, Lk 4:29, Jo 4:8, al. mult.; opp. to κῶμαι (κ. καὶ ἀγροί), Mt 9:3510:11, Mk 6:56, Lk 8:113:22; c. nom. propr. in appos. (cl.), Ac 11:516:14; c. id. in gen. appos. (Bl., § 35, 5), Ac 8:5, II Pe 2:6; gen., of the region, Lk 1:264:31, Jo 4:5; of the inhabitants, Mt 10:5, 23, Lk 23:51, Ac 19:35, II Co 11:32; c. gen. pers., of one's residence or native place, Mt 22:7, Lk 2:4, 114:2910:11, Jo 1:45, Ac 16:20, Re 16:9; of Jerusalem: ἡ ἁγία π., Mt 4:527:53, Re 11:2; ἡ ἠγαπημένη, Re 20:19; π. τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως, Mt 5:35 (cf. Ps 47 (48):2); of the heavenly city in the Apocalyptic visions, Re 3:1221:2, 10, 14 ff. 22:14, 19. By meton., of the inhabitants of a city: Mt 8:3412:2521:10, Mk 1:33, Ac 14:2121:30.

ποταμός.sd: a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water
ποταμός.der: probably from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω) (compare G4224 (πότος));
ποταμός.as:
ποταμός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for נָהָר, יְאֹר;]
a river, stream, torrent: Mt 3:57:25, 27, Mk 1:5, Lk 6:48, 49, Ac 16:13, II Co 11:26, Re 8:109:1412:15, 1616:4, 1221:1, 2. Fig., pl., π. ὕδατος ζῶντος, Jo 7:38.†

πούς.as:
πούς, ποδός, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for רֶגֶל;]
a foot, both of men and beasts: Mt 4:6(LXX), Mk 9:45, Lk 1:79, Jo 11:44, Ac 7:5, al.; ὑπο τοὺς π., Ro 16:20, I Co 15:25, 27, Eph 1:22, He 2:8; ὑποκάτω τῶν π., Mt 22:44(LXX); πρὸς (παρὰ) τοὺς π., Mk 5:22, Lk 8:41, al.; fig., Mt 15:30, Lk 10:39, Ac 5:2, al.; ἔμπροσθεν τῶν π., Re 3:919:10, al.; ἐπὶ τοὺς π., Ac 10:25. By meton., of a person in motion (Ps 118 (119):101): Lk 1:79, Ac 5:9, Ro 3:1510:15, He 12:13.

ποικίλος.long: various, of different colors, diverse, various.
ποικίλος.as:
ποικίλος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX for נָקֹד, רִקְמָה, etc.;]
many-coloured, variegated. Metaph., various, manifold: Mt 4:24, Mk 1:34, Lk 4:40, II Ti 3:6, Tit 3:3, He 2:413:9, Ja 1:2, I Pe 1:64:10.†

πονηρός.sd: hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from G2556 (κακός), which refers rather to essential character, as well as from G4550 (σαπρός), which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners
πονηρός.kj: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness)
πονηρός.as:
πονηρός, -ά, -όν
(< πονέω, to toil), [in LXX chiefly for רַע;]
1.
(a) of persons, oppressed by toils (Hes.);
(b) of things, toilsome, painful (καιρός, Si 51:12): Eph 5:166:13, Re 16:2.
2.bad, worthless;
(a) in physical sense: καρπός, Mt 7:17, 18;
(b) in ethical sense, bad, evil, wicked;
(α) of persons: Mt 7:1112:34, 3518:3225:26, Lk 6:4511:1319:22, Ac 17:5, II Th 3:2, II Ti 3:13; γενεά, Mt 12:39, 4516:4, Lk 11:29; πνεῦμια, Mt 12:45, Lk 7:218:211:26, Ac 19:12, 13, 15, 16; as subst., οἱ π., opp. to δίκαιοι, Mt 13:49; to ἀγαθοί, Mt 5:4522:10; οἱ ἀχάριστοι καὶ π., Lk 6:35; sing., ὁ π., Mt 5:39, I Co 5:13; id. esp. of Satan, the evil one, Mt 5:376:13 (v. Lft., Notes, 125 ff.; but cf. McN, in l.) 13:19, 38, Lk 11:4 (WH, R, om.), Jo 17:15, Eph 6:16, II Th 3:3 (Lft., Notes, 125 ff.), I Jo 2:13, 143:125:18, 19;
(β) of things: Mt 5:1112:3515:19, Lk 6:22, 45, Jo 3:197:7, Ac 18:1425:18, Ga 1:4, Col 1:21, I Ti 6:4, II Ti 4:18, He 3:1210:22, Ja 2:44:16, I Jo 3:12, II Jo 11, III Jo 10; ὀφθαλμός (q.v.), Mt 6:2320:15, Mk 7:22, Lk 11:34; as subst., neut., τὸ π., Ac 28:21, I Th 5:22; opp. to ἀγαθόν, Lk 6:45, Ro 12:9; pl., Mt 9:4, Mk 7:23, Lk 3:19.†
SYN.: v.s. ἄθεσμος.

πορνεία.sd: harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry
πορνεία.as:
πορνεία, -ας, ἡ
(< πορνεύω), [in LXX for זְנוּנִים, תַּזְנוּת and cogn. forms;]
fornication: Ac 15:20, 2921:25, I Co 5:16:13, 18, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19, Eph 5:3, Col 3:5, I Th 4:3 (Lft., Notes, 53), Re 9:21; pl. (v. WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), I Co 7:2; disting. from μοιχεία, Mt 15:19, Mk 7:21; = μοιχεία (Am 8:17, Si 23:23, al.), Mt 5:3219:9. Metaph. (of idolatry: De 23:2, Ho 1:2): Jo 8:41 (Westc., in l.), and so perh. (Thayer-Grimm, s.v.; but v. Swete, in ll.), Re 2:2114:1817:2, 418:319:2.†

πολυλογία.der: from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3056 (λόγος);
πολυλογία.as:
πολυλογία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX: Pr 10:19 (דְּבָרִיםרֹב)*;]
much speaking, loquacity: Mt 6:7.†

πόσος.g: how much, how great, how many
πόσος.long: how much, how great, how many.
πόσος.sd: interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many)
πόσος.der: from an absolute (who, what) and G3739 (ὅς);
πόσος.as:
πόσος, -η, -ον,
adj. of number, magnitude, degree, etc.,
how much, how great, how many: Mt 6:23, II Co 7:11; of time, Mk 9:21; neut., absol., Lk 16:5, 7; dat., πόσῳ, adverbially, how much, Mt 12:12; id. seq. μᾶλλον, Mt 7:1110:25, Lk 11:1312:24, 28, Ro 11:12, 24, Phm 16, He 9:14; π. χείρονος τιμωρίας, He 10:29; pl., Mt 15:3416:9, 1027:13, Mk 6:388:5, 19, 2015:4, Lk 15:17, Ac 21:20.†

ποταπός.long: of what kind, of what manner.
ποταπός.sd: interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort
ποταπός.der: apparently from G4219 (πότε) and the base of G4226 (ποῦ);
ποταπός.as:
** ποταπός
(late form of cl. ποδ-), -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Da LXX Su 54*;]
1. (= ποδαπός) from what country?
2. In late writers, = ποῖος, of what sort?: Mt 8:27, Mk 13:1, Lk 1:297:39, II Pe 3:11, I Jo 3:1.†

ποιμήν.long: a shepherd; hence met: of the feeder, protector, and ruler of a flock of men.
ποιμήν.as:
ποιμήν, -ένος, ὁ,
[in LXX for רֹעֶה;]
a shepherd: Mt 9:3625:3226:31(LXX), Mk 6:3414:27, Lk 2:8, 15, 18, 20, Jo 10:2, 12. Metaph., of Christ; Jo 10:11, 14, 16, He 13:20, I Pe 2:25; of Christian pastors, Eph 4:11 (cf. Hom., Il., i, 263, ποιμένα λαῶν).†

ποτίζω.g: I cause to drink, give to drink
ποτίζω.long: I cause to drink, give to drink; irrigate, water.
ποτίζω.der: from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω);
ποτίζω.as:
ποτίζω
(< πότος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקה hi.;]
to give to drink: c. acc. pers., Mt 25:35, 37, 4227:48, Mk 15:36, Lk 13:15, Ro 12:20; c. dupl. acc., Mt 10:42, Mk 9:41; fig., γάλα, I Co 3:2; ἐκ τ. οἴνου, Re 14:8; of plants, to water (Xen., Strab., al.; Ge 13:10), fig., I Co 3:6-8. Metaph. (cf. Is 29:10, Si 15:3), of the Spirit, I Co 12:13.†

ποτήριον.long: a drinking cup, the contents of the cup; fig: the portion which God allots.
ποτήριον.sd: a drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate
ποτήριον.der: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω);
ποτήριον.as:
ποτήριον, -ου, τό, dimin. of ποτήρ
(< πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹס;]
a wine cup: Mt 23:25, 2626:27, Mk 7:414:23, Lk 11:3922:17, 20a (WH, R, mg., om.), I Co 11:25, Re 17:4; πίνειν ἐκ τοῦ π., I Co 11:28; c. gen. rei, Mt 10:42, Mk 9:41; τ. εὐλογίας, I Co 10:16; by meton., of the contents of the cup, Lk 22:20b (WH, R, mg., om.), I Co 11:25, 26; c. gen. pers., I Co 10:2111:27. Metaph., of experience of divine providence; of prosperity (Ps 15 (16):5, al.); of adversity (Ps 10 (11):6, Is 51:17, al.): of the sufferings of Christ, Mt 20:22, 2326:3910:38, 3914:36, Lk 22:42, Jo 18:11; of divine punishment, Re 14:1016:1918:6.†

πόθεν.sd: from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause
πόθεν.der: from the base of G4213 (πόσις) with enclitic adverb of origin;
πόθεν.as:
πόθεν,
adv.,
whence;
(a) of place: Mt 15:33, Lk 13:25, 27, Jo 3:86:58:149:29, 3019:9, Re 7:13; metaph., of condition, Re 2:5;
(b) of origin: Mt 13:27, 54, 5621:25, Mk 6:2, Lk 20:7, Jo 2:9, Ja 4:1; of parentage, Jo 7:27, 28;
(c) of cause: Mk 8:412:37, Lk 1:43, Jo 1:494:11.†

πολύτιμος.long: of great value, very costly, very precious.
πολύτιμος.as:
* πολύτιμος, -ον
(< πολύς, τιμή),
1.much revered (Menand.).
2.very costly, very precious: Mt 13:4626:7 (βαρύτιμος, WH), Jo 12:3; comparat., I Pe 1:7.†

πόρρω.long: far, far off, at a distance.
πόρρω.as:
πόρρω,
adv.
(in older Attic, πρόσω), [in LXX for רָחוֹק, etc.;]
far off: Mt 15:8, Mk 7:6(LXX), Lk 14:32; comparat., πορρώτερον (-ρω, T), Lk 24:28.†

πότε.der: from the base of G4226 (ποῦ) and G5037 (τέ);
πότε.as:
πότε,
interrog. adv. of time,
when?: Mt 25:37-39, 44, Lk 21:7, Jo 6:25; ἕως π., how long: Mt 17:17, Mk 9:19, Lk 9:41, Jo 10:24, Re 6:10. In indir. questions, = ὁπότε, Mt 24:3, Mk 13:4, 33, 35, Lk 12:3617:20 (v. Bl., § 25, 4).†

ποσάκις.as:
ποσάκις,
interrog. num. adv.,
how often: Mt 18:2123:37, Lk 13:34.†

ποῖος.sd: individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one
ποῖος.der: from the base of G4226 (ποῦ) and G3634 (οἷος);
ποῖος.as:
ποῖος, -α, -ον,
interrog. pronom. adj.
(corresponding to the demonstr. τοῖος and the relat. οἷος), [in LXX chiefly for אֵי־זֶה;]
of what quality or sort: absol., n. pl., Lk 24:19; c. subst.;
(a) prop., in direct questions: Mt 19:1821:2322:3624:42, Mk 11:2812:28, Lk 6:32-34, Jo 10:32, Ac 4:77:49, Ro 3:27, I Co 15:35, Ja 4:14 (but v.s. ποία), I Pe 2:20;
(b) in indirect questions = ὁποῖος: Mt 21:24, 2724:43, Mk 11:29, 33, Lk 12:3920:2, 8, Jo 12:3318:3221:19, Ac 23:34, I Pe 1:11, Re 3:3; ποίας (sc. ὁδοῦ), Lk 5:19.†

πόρνη.long: a prostitute; met: an idolatrous community.
πόρνη.as:
πόρνη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for זוֹנָה;]
a prostitute, harlot: Mt 21:31, 32, Lk 15:30, I Co 6:15, 16, He 11:31, Ja 2:25. Metaph. (v. Swete, Ap., 180 f.), of Babylon (i.e. Rome): Re 17:1, 5, 17:15, 1619:2.†

πονηρία.sd: depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins
πονηρία.as:
πονηρία, -ας, ἡ
(< πονηρός), [in LXX chiefly for רָעָה;]
iniquity, wickedness: Mt 22:18, Lk 11:39, Ro 1:29, Eph 6:12; pl. (v. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220; Swete, Mk., 153), Mk 7:22, Ac 3:26; κακία καὶ π., I Co 5:8.†
SYN.: v.s. κακία.

πόλεμος.sd: warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series)
πόλεμος.as:
πόλεμος, -ον, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מִלְחָמָה;]
1.war: Mt 24:6, Mk 13:7, Lk 14:3121:9, He 11:34; π. ποιεῖν, seq. μετά, c. gen. (cf. πολεμέω), Re 11:712:1713:719:19.
2. = μάχη, a fight, battle: I Co 14:8, Re 9:7, 912:716:1420:8; hyperb., of private quarrels (cf. πολεμέω), Ja 4:1.†

ποίμνη.as:
ποίμνη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ge 32:16 (17) (עֵדֶר), Za 13:7 A*;]
a flock, prop., of sheep: Mt 26:31, Lk 2:8, I Co 9:7. Metaph., of Christ's followers, Jo 10:16.†

πολυτελής.long: very costly, very precious, of great value.
πολυτελής.kj: costly, very precious, of great price
πολυτελής.as:
πολυτελής, -ές
(< πολύς, τέλος), [in LXX for יָקָר, etc.;]
very costly, very precious, of great value: Mk 14:3, I Ti 2:9; metaph., I Pe 3:4.†

πορφύρα.long: a purple garment, indicating power or wealth.
πορφύρα.sd: the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it
πορφύρα.as:
πορφύρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן, אַרְגְּוָן;]
1.the purple-fish (cf. I Mac 4:23).
2.purple dye.
3. Later, = πορφυρίς, a purple garment: Mk 15:17, 20, Lk 16:19, Re 18:12.†

Πόντιος.as:
Πόντιος, -ου, ὁ,
Pontius, the prænomen of Pilate (v.s. Πειλᾶτος), Mt 27:2 (Rec., WH, mg.), Lk 3:1, Ac 4:27, I Ti 6:13.†

ποίμνιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4167 (ποίμνη);
ποίμνιον.as:
ποίμνιον, -ου, τό, = ποίμνη, q.v.,
[in LXX chiefly for עֹאן, also for עֵדֶר, etc.;]
a flock, prop., of sheep. Metaph., of Christians: Lk 12:32, Ac 20:28, 29, I Pe 5:3; τ. θεοῦ, I Pe 5:2.†

πορεία.sd: travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career
πορεία.as:
πορεία, -ας, ἡ
(< πορεύω), [in LXX chiefly for הֲלִיכָה and cogn. forms;]
1.a journey: Lk 13:22.
2.a going: metaph. ("the rich man perishes while he is still on the move," Hort., in l.), Ja 1:11.†

πολίτης.as:
πολίτης, -ου, ὁ
(< πόλις), [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ;]
1.a citizen: c. gen. loc., Lk 15:15, Ac 21:39.
2.a fellow-citizen: c. gen. pers., Lk 19:14, He 8:11(LXX).†

πόρρωθεν.long: from afar, far off, from a distance.
πόρρωθεν.sd: from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly
πόρρωθεν.der: from G4206 (πόῤῥω) with adverbial enclitic of source;
πόρρωθεν.as:
πόρρωθεν,
adv.
(< τόρρω, q.v.), [in LXX for מֵרָחוֹק and cogn. forms;]
from afar: Lk 17:12, He 11:13.†

πολλαπλασίων.sd: manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more
πολλαπλασίων.der: from G4183 (πολύς) and probably a derivative of G4120 (πλέκω);
πολλαπλασίων.as:
*† πολλαπλασίων, -ον
(< πόλυς),
= πολλαπλάσιος, many times more: Mt 19:29, Lk 18:30.†

ποτέ.long: at one time or other, at some time, formerly.
ποτέ.sd: indefinite adverb, at some time, ever
ποτέ.kj: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when
ποτέ.der: from the base of G4225 (πού) and G5037 (τέ);
ποτέ.as:
ποτέ,
enclitic particle,
1.once, formerly, sometime: of the past, Jo 9:13, Ro 7:911:30, Ga 1:13, 232:6 (Lft., in l.), Eph 2:2, 3, 11, 135:8, Col 1:213:7, I Th 2:5, Tit 3:3, Phm 11, I Pe 2:103:5, 20; ἤδη ποτέ, now at length, Phl 4:10; of the fut., Lk 22:32; εἴ πως ἤδη ποτέ, if sometime soon at length, Ro 1:10.
2.ever: after a neg., Eph 5:29, II Pe 1:10, 21; in a question, τίς π., I Co 9:7, He 1:5, 13.†

πόσις.sd: a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught
πόσις.as:
πόσις, -εως, ἡ
(< πίνω), [in LXX: Da, LXX TH 1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה)*;]
1. prop., drinking: Ro 14:17, Col 2:16 (v. Lft.; ICC, in l.).
2. = πόμα, drink: Jo 6:55 (cf. βρῶσις).†

πότερον.sd: interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that
πότερον.der: neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226 (ποῦ);
πότερον.as:
πότερος, -α, -ον,
which of two. Neut., adverbially, πότερον, whether: Jo 7:17.†

πορφυροῦς.as:
πορφύρεος, -α, -ον, contr., -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν
(< πορφύρα), [in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן;]
purple: Jo 19:2, 5; as subst., πορφυροῦν (sc. ἱμάτιον), Re 17:418:6.†

Πόντος.long: Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor, bordering on the Black Sea, governed along with Bithynia.
Πόντος.sd: a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor
Πόντος.as:
Πόντος, -ου, ὁ,
Pontus, a region of Asia Minor, bordering on the πόντος Εὔξεινος: Ac 2:9, I Pe 1:1.†

πορθέω.long: I lay waste, destroy, ravage, harass.
πορθέω.as:
** πορθέω collat. form (in cl. chiefly poët.) of πέρθω,
[in LXX: IV Mac 4:2311:4*;]
to destroy, ravage: Ac 9:21, Ga 1:13, 23.†

Πόλις.long: a city, the inhabitants of a city.
Πόλις.sd: a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size)
Πόλις.der: probably from the same as G4171 (πόλεμος), or perhaps from G4183 (πολύς);
Πόλις.as:
πόλις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for עִיר;]
a city: Mt 2:23, Mk 1:45, Lk 4:29, Jo 4:8, al. mult.; opp. to κῶμαι (κ. καὶ ἀγροί), Mt 9:3510:11, Mk 6:56, Lk 8:113:22; c. nom. propr. in appos. (cl.), Ac 11:516:14; c. id. in gen. appos. (Bl., § 35, 5), Ac 8:5, II Pe 2:6; gen., of the region, Lk 1:264:31, Jo 4:5; of the inhabitants, Mt 10:5, 23, Lk 23:51, Ac 19:35, II Co 11:32; c. gen. pers., of one's residence or native place, Mt 22:7, Lk 2:4, 114:2910:11, Jo 1:45, Ac 16:20, Re 16:9; of Jerusalem: ἡ ἁγία π., Mt 4:527:53, Re 11:2; ἡ ἠγαπημένη, Re 20:19; π. τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως, Mt 5:35 (cf. Ps 47 (48):2); of the heavenly city in the Apocalyptic visions, Re 3:1221:2, 10, 14 ff. 22:14, 19. By meton., of the inhabitants of a city: Mt 8:3412:2521:10, Mk 1:33, Ac 14:2121:30.

πορφυρόπωλις.g: a female seller of purple cloth
πορφυρόπωλις.long: a female seller of purple cloth.
πορφυρόπωλις.sd: a female trader in purple cloth
πορφυρόπωλις.der: feminine of a compound of G4209 (πορφύρα) and G4453 (πωλέω);
πορφυρόπωλις.as:
*† πορφυρόπωλις, -ιδος, ἡ,
a seller of purple fabrics: Ac 16:14.†

πολιτάρχης.long: a ruler of a city, city magistrate.
πολιτάρχης.as:
*† πολιτάρχης, -ου, ὁ,
= πολίαρχος (Pind., Eur.),
the ruler of a city, a politarch: Ac 17:6, 8 (v. MM, xx).†

ποιητής.long: (a) a "maker," poet, (b) a doer, carrier out, performer.
ποιητής.as:
** ποιητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ποιέω), [in LXX: I Mac 2:67*;]
1. in cl., a maker, author.
2. Esp., a poet: Ac 17:28.
3. Later, a doer: τ. νόμου, Ro 2:13, Ja 4:11 (I Mac 2:67); ἔργου, Ja 1:25; λόγου, Ja 1:22, 23.†

Ποντικός.sd: a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus

πολιτεία.long: (a) commonwealth, polity; citizen body, (b) (the Roman) citizenship, citizen-rights, franchise.
πολιτεία.as:
** πολιτεία, -ας, ἡ
(< πολιτεύω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:116:238:1713:14, III Mac 3:21, 23, IV Mac 3:208:717:9*;]
1.citizenship: Ac 22:28 (III Mac 3:21, 23, Hdt., Xen., a1.).
2.government, administration (Aristoph., Dem., al.).
3.a commonwealth: Eph 2:12.†

πολιτεύομαι.g: I live the life of a citizen
πολιτεύομαι.long: I live the life of a citizen, live.
πολιτεύομαι.der: middle voice of a derivative of G4177 (πολίτης);
πολιτεύομαι.as:
** πολιτεύω, more freq. as depon., -ομαι, and so in LXX and NT
(< πολίτης), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 6:111:25, III Mac 3:4, IV Mac4*;]
to be a citizen, live as a citizen: metaph., of conduct as based on heavenly citizenship, Ac 23:1, Phl 1:27.†

Πόρκιος.long: Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus.
Πόρκιος.as:
Πόρκιος, -ου, ὁ,
Porcius, prænomen of Porcius Festus (v.s. Φῆστος): Ac 24:27.†

πού.long: where, somewhere, anywhere; with numerals: somewhere about.
πού.sd: as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly
πού.der: genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214 (πόσος));
πού.as:
πού,
enclitic particle,
1.anywhere, somewhere: He 2:64:4.
2.in some degree, perhaps, about: Ac 27:29 (T, μήπου), Ro 4:19; δή που (T, δήπου), surely: He 2:16.†

Ποτίολοι.long: Puteoli, the great harbor for traffic with Alexandria on the Bay of Naples.
Ποτίολοι.sd: little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy
Ποτίολοι.as:
Ποτίολοι, -ων, οἱ,
Puteoli (mod. Pozzuoli), a city on the Bay of Naples: Ac 28:13.†

ποίημα.long: a thing made, a work, workmanship.
ποίημα.sd: a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively)
ποίημα.as:
ποίημα, -τος, τό
(< ποιέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה (freq. in Ec);]
that which is made or done, a work: Ro 1:20, Eph 2:10.†

πόρνος.long: a fornicator, man who prostitutes himself.
πόρνος.sd: akin to the base of G4097 (πιπράσκω)); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine)
πόρνος.as:
** πόρνος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Si 23:16-18*;]
1.a male prostitute (Xen., al.).
2.a fornicator: I Co 5:9-116:9, Eph 5:5, I Ti 1:10, He 12:1513:4, Re 21:822:15.†

πορνεύω.long: I fornicate; met: I practice idolatry.
πορνεύω.sd: to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry
πορνεύω.as:
πορνεύω,
[in LXX for זנה;]
1.to prostitute the body for hire.
2.to commit fornication: Mk 10:19 (WH, mg), I Co 6:1810:8, Re 2:14, 20. Metaph. (as in LXX: I Ch 5:25, Je 3:6, Ho 9:1, al.), of idolatry (but v. Swete, Ap., 180 f.), Re 17:218:3, 9 (cf. ἐκ-πορνεύω).†

πόμα.as:
πόμα, -τος, τό
(< πίνω), late form of Att. πῶμα, [in LXX: Ps 101 (102):9 (שִׁקּוּי), al.4*;]
drink: I Co 10:4, He 9:10.†

πολυποίκιλος.as:
* πολυ-ποίκιλος, -ον,
1.much variegated, of greatly differing colours (Eur.).
2.manifold: Eph 3:10.†

πολίτευμα.as:
** πολίτευμα, -τος, τό
(< πολιτεύω), [in LXX: II Mac 12:7*;]
1.an act of administration.
2.a form of government.
3. = πολιτεία,
(a)citizenship: Phl 3:20 (R, txt.);
(b)community, commonwealth: Phl 3:20 (R, mg.; for exx. v. MM, xx).†

πόνος.long: (a) labor, toil, (b) pain, anguish, distress, suffering.
πόνος.as:
πόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for עָמָל, etc.;]
1.labour, toil: Col 4:13.
2. The consequence of toil, distress, suffering, pain (Xen., al., LXX): Re 16:10, 1121:4.†
SYN.: v.s. κόπος.

πορισμός.der: from a derivative of (a way, i.e. means);
πορισμός.as:
**† πορισμός, -ου, ὁ
(< πορίζω, to procure), [in LXX: Wi 13:1914:2*;]
1.a providing.
2.a means of gain: I Ti 6:5, 6 (Polyb., al.).†

Πούδης.long: Pudens, a Christian man in Rome.
Πούδης.as:
Πούδης
(in π., gen. -εντος, v. Zorell, s.v.), ὁ (Latin),
Pudens: II Ti 4:21.†

πολυμερῶς.long: in many parts (one at one time, another at another, and so on).
πολυμερῶς.sd: in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal)
πολυμερῶς.der: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3313 (μέρος);
πολυμερῶς.as:
*† πολυμερῶς,
adv.
(< πολύς, μέρος),
in many parts or portions: He 1:1 (Plut., al.).†

πολυτρόπως.sd: in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form
πολυτρόπως.der: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G5158 (τρόπος);
πολυτρόπως.as:
** πολυτρόπως,
adv.
(< πολύτροπος, 1. much turning. 2. manifold), [in LXX: IV Mac 3:21 A*;]
in many ways or manners: He 1:1 (Philo).†

ποίησις.as:
ποίησις, -εως, ἡ
(ποιέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה and cognate forms;]
1.a making (Hdt., Thuc., al.).
2.a doing (Si 19:1851:19): Ja 1:25.†

πολεμέω.long: I make war, contend, fight, battle.
πολεμέω.sd: to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively)
πολεμέω.as:
πολεμέω, -ῶ
(< πόλεμος), [in LXX chiefly for לחם ni.;]
to make war, fight: Re 12:7b19:11; seq. μετά (II Ki 21:15 and v. M, Pr., 106, 247), Re 2:1612:7a13:417:14; hyperb., of private quarrels, Ja 4:2.†

πότος.as:
πότος, -ου, ὁ
(< πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁתֶּה;]
a drinking bout, carousal: I Pe 4:3.†
SYN.: v.s. κραιπάλη.

ποδήρης.long: reaching to the feet (of a garment).
ποδήρης.sd: a dress (G2066 (ἐσθής) implied) reaching the ankles
ποδήρης.der: from G4228 (πούς) and another element of uncertain affinity;
ποδήρης.as:
ποδήρης, -ες
(< πούς), [in LXX: Ex 25:6 (7) 35:9 (חֹשֶׁן), 28:429:5 (מְעִיל), 28:27 (31) (אֵפוֹד), Ez 9:2, 3, 11 (בַּד), Za 3:5 (4) (מַחֲלָצוֹת), Wi 18:24, Si 27:845:8*;]
reaching to the feet: of a garment (sc. χιτών, cf. Ex 25:6 (7) 28:4, 27 (31) 29:535:9, Ez 9:2, 3, 11; Xen., al.), Re 1:13 (for -η, LT7 read -ην; v. M, Pr., 49).†
SYN.: στολή, v. Tr., Syn., § 1.

ποταμοφόρητος.sd: river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream
ποταμοφόρητος.der: from G4215 (ποταμός) and a derivative of G5409 (φορέω);
ποταμοφόρητος.as:
*† ποταμο-φόρητος, -ον,
carried away by a stream: Re 12:15 (for two exx. in π., v. MM, xxi).†
